intro: Long ago, surfers in California had a problem. Some days the ocean had no waves. So people put roller-skate wheels under a wooden board. They rolled on the sidewalk instead.
In this unit, you will learn how the skateboard began. You will meet the parts of a board. You will learn the job of each part, from the deck to the tiny bearings.
By the end, you can tell the story of the first boards. You can point to each part and say what it does. You can check a board with a grown-up before a ride.
bigQuestion: How did people make a board that rolls, and what does each part do?

timeline.t: California surfers ride wooden boards with roller-skate wheels
Stores begin to sell ready-made skateboards
Larry Stevenson starts making Makaha skateboards
First national skateboard championships in Anaheim, California
Champion Patti McGee is on the cover of Life magazine
Frank Nasworthy sells soft plastic wheels called Cadillac Wheels
Carlsbad Skatepark in California and Skateboard City in Florida open
Skateboarding is added to the Olympic Games
Skateboarding is in the Olympics for the first time, in Tokyo, Japan

words.d: to ride a wave on a long board in the ocean
an early name for skateboarding, because it felt like surfing on land
shoes or frames with wheels on the bottom
the board of a skateboard that you stand on
the front end and the back end of the deck
a rough, sticky sheet on top of the deck that keeps shoes from slipping
the metal parts under the deck that hold the wheels and help the board turn
a small metal ring with tiny balls inside that helps a wheel spin

test.q: Why did surfers start riding boards on land?
choices: Some days the ocean had no waves
test.why: On flat days there were no waves to ride, so surfers rode boards with wheels on land.

test.q: What wheels did people use on the first homemade boards?
test.why: People took wheels off roller skates and fixed them under a wooden board.

test.q: Who invented the very first skateboard?
test.why: There are many stories, but no single inventor is known.

test.q: Why did people call it sidewalk surfing?
choices: It was done in the ocean
It felt like surfing, but on land
test.why: Riders leaned and turned like surfers, but on paths and sidewalks.

test.q: About when did stores start to sell skateboards?
test.why: Ready-made boards were sold in stores around 1959.

test.q: In 2021, skateboarding was in what big games for the first time?
test.why: Skateboarding was first in the Olympics in 2021, in Tokyo, Japan.
The deck is the flat board you stand on.

test.q: Which part keeps your shoes from slipping?
test.why: Grip tape is rough like sandpaper, so shoes hold tight.

test.q: Which parts tilt when you lean so the board turns?
test.why: Trucks tilt when you lean, so the wheels point a new way and the board turns.

test.q: What do bearings help the wheels do?
test.why: Bearings have tiny steel balls inside that help the wheels spin.

write.prompt: Tell how the skateboard began. Then pick two parts of a skateboard. Say what each part is and what job it does.
tips: Start with the surfers and the flat ocean.
Say what the first boards were made of.
Use part names like deck, trucks, wheels or grip tape.
For each part, tell its job in one sentence.
